conclusion: smallest tested N per arm meeting P(BLOCK) >= 0.8: 400 (800 trials in total).
assumptions: This is planning under assumptions, not observed power: the true success rates are inputs, not measurements.
Independent binomial arms: each arm is N independent trials at its stated true rate.
No pairing: shared seeds or any other dependence between the arms is not modelled.
Fixed sample: one look at N per arm, no early stopping and no extension.
One gating condition (K=1), no trial ERROR and no candidate hard-invariant violation; either of those overrides the rates in the real gate.
The gate's exact rule: two-sided Clopper-Pearson per arm with tail alpha/(4K), bounds [L_B - U_A, U_B - L_A] on the difference, PASS iff L > -delta, BLOCK iff U < -delta, otherwise INCONCLUSIVE.
Probabilities enumerate every pair of success counts; they are not simulated. They need not rise monotonically with N, so only the tested N values are claimed.
